title: MCP Shield: security scanner for AI-agent tool connections
source: Top 25 SaaS ideas for Victor (research report, Nov 2026)
summary: A free command-line scanner, with a paid team dashboard, that checks the MCP servers developers plug into AI coding agents for poisoned tool descriptions, too-broad permissions and leaked secrets.
hook: "Our developers installed a dozen MCP servers into their AI agents last month. I have no idea what those tools can do."
story:
**Lukas is head of engineering at an 80-person software company.** His developers use Claude Code and Cursor, and each one has plugged in several MCP servers: database tools, GitHub, Slack, random open-source tools found online.

The security team asks: **which tools have access to what?** Could a tool description contain hidden instructions? Are API keys sitting in plain-text config files? The enterprise MCP gateways on the market are heavy to deploy. Lukas wants a **simple scanner** his developers can run, and one dashboard that shows the risks across the team.
whyNow: Investors are pouring money into the space: Runlayer launched with an $11M seed in November 2025 and Obot raised a $35M seed. The OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications lists prompt injection and "excessive agency" among the main risks. MCP (the Model Context Protocol) is now the standard way to connect tools to AI assistants such as Claude Code or Cursor.
evidence: Runlayer launched with an $11M seed in November 2025 [TechCrunch]
Obot AI raised a $35M seed for an enterprise MCP gateway [VCA Online]
Archestra raised $3.3M (Aug 2025) to secure enterprise use of MCP servers [SiliconANGLE]
Helmet Security emerged from stealth with $9M in funding [SecurityWeek]
OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications lists prompt injection and excessive agency among main risks [OWASP]
Pain evidence is indirect: investor money and the OWASP list, not customer surveys [Top 25 report]
